newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes hold gains, led by sweet "squeeze".
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes hold gains, led by sweet "squeeze".

text.p: U.S. crudes racked up further gains Wednesday, with a squeeze on refiners behind the advances in outright prices and differentials, traders said.
The market for 'sweet' crudes led the way and 'sour' grades, though holding most of their recent strength, fell from the day's best levels by late in the session.
Benchmark West Texas Intermediate at Cushing, Texas was up about 35 cents on the day at $26.00/10 at 1800 EST.
"There is still a squeeze on the sweet market," said an oil trader with a large trading house. "Refiners are short and need to cover," he said.

In a topsy-turvy day, crude prices started off softer and differentials, apart from those for Gulf sours, were steady to weaker as product prices gave up ground on a less bullish outlook for the weather in the eastern part of the country.
But the afternoon saw renewed buying and the squeeze was evidenced by a turnaround in the futures, though not confined to the exchange.
Among actively traded physical grades, WTI/Midland was last seen traded at a three-cent premium to marker WTI/Cushing and bid there again, brokers said. That was up from around evens on Tuesday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James was holding above 60 cents premium to the marker, while HLS/Empire was trading at around a 10 cent premium, little changed on the day.

In the sour market, a sharp narrowing in the discount in recent days was aided as Mobil Corp announced that its Green Canyon platform in the Gulf of Mexico would be out of service for two to three months as a result of a fire at the facility last week.
The platform produces around 21,800 barrels per day (bpd) of oil, which feeds into the Texaco-operated Eugene Island facility.
Eugene Island crude itself was not seen active but was bid at a $1.00 discount, compared with $1.15/$1.05 on Tuesday, brokers said.

The West Texas Sour/Midland market, which was trading close to a $2 discount a couple of weeks ago, traded as high as 95 cents below WTI/Cushing on Wednesday, but slipped back to $1.30/$1.20 below late in the day.
